name: North American X-15
notes: Air-launched rocket plane. Record 107.96 km altitude and Mach 6.7. Thirteen flights exceeded 50 miles (astronaut wings).

name: X-20 Dyna-Soar
notes: Boost-glide orbital spaceplane cancelled in 1963 before first flight.

name: SpaceShipOne
notes: First private crewed spaceflight (Jun 2004); won the Ansari X Prize (4 Oct 2004, 112 km).

name: SpaceShipTwo VSS Unity
notes: Air-launched suborbital tourist spaceplane; retired 2024 in favour of Delta-class ships.

name: Boeing X-37B
notes: Reusable uncrewed orbital test vehicle operated by the US Space Force; missions last years.

name: McDonnell Douglas DC-X
notes: Vertical-takeoff-and-landing prototype that pioneered rapid turnaround reusable rocketry.

name: SpaceX Grasshopper
notes: VTVL test vehicle with Merlin 1D; hop to 744 m; predecessor of Falcon 9 booster landing.

name: HOTOL
notes: 1980s single-stage-to-orbit spaceplane concept; cancelled 1988. Precursor to Skylon.

name: Skylon
notes: Uncrewed single-stage-to-orbit spaceplane using SABRE synergistic air-breathing rocket engines; engine tests continue, vehicle unbuilt.

name: Sänger Silbervogel
notes: 1930s–40s antipodal bomber concept: rocket sled launch, skip-glide trajectory. Never built.

name: Project Orion (nuclear pulse)
notes: 1958–65 design propelled by detonating small nuclear charges behind a pusher plate. Proof-of-concept 'Put-Put' flew on conventional explosives (1959). Partial Test Ban Treaty ended it.

name: NERVA / Project Rover
notes: Ground-tested nuclear thermal rocket engines (1955–72), never flown. Isp ≈ 2× best chemical engines. Cancelled 1973.

name: Project Daedalus
notes: 1973–78 unmanned interstellar probe study to Barnard's Star (5.9 ly) at ~12% of light speed in ~50 years; two stages with ~50,000 t of fuel.

name: Project Longshot
notes: 1988 unmanned probe concept to Alpha Centauri, ~100-year transit.

name: Breakthrough Starshot
notes: Proposed gram-scale 'StarChip' light sails pushed by a ~100 GW ground laser to ~20% light speed; reach Alpha Centauri in ~20 years.

name: IKAROS
notes: First spacecraft to demonstrate solar sail propulsion in interplanetary space.

name: Deep Space 1
notes: First interplanetary use of ion propulsion; flew by comet Borrelly.

name: Alcubierre warp drive
notes: Speculative general-relativity solution for faster-than-light travel; requires negative energy density. Included as a sim-level fantasy option, not a buildable design.
